posts.title: Fail Safe Logic
posts.author: Admin
posts.excerpt: Fail Safe Logic in each project often not goes to advance level.
posts.content:
Introduction

In almost all the project, fail safe design and logic is given less importance and carried out only for customer satisfaction. Any Fail Safe logic must have details like which Safety Category has been adopted, how it is designed and how it is going to be executed. Customer will be more curious and will realize how serious are we about safety. Wiring E-Stop to safety relay or PLC often goes with theory logic. This must be analyzed in detail, designer need to adopt a system to understand what type of safety ,customer requires or if he is not aware, based on project 3D CAD needs to present safety category adopted in design.

posts.title: Engineer Performance Matrix — How the Score Is Calculated
posts.author: Admin
posts.excerpt: Methodology behind the Skill Matrix score and the 'Engineers Needing Support' panel — data sources, formula, worked examples, and the HR justification framework for recruiting or outsourcing.
posts.content:
DRB TechVerse — Controls Team Dashboard · Prepared for HR / Management Review · July 2026

This article explains exactly how the score behind the Skill Matrix page and its “Engineers Needing Support” panel is calculated, and how a low score translates into a defensible business case for recruiting or outsourcing an additional engineer.

1. Purpose

The Skill Matrix page flags certain engineers under “Engineers Needing Support”, showing the engineer’s name, score, and an automatic diagnosis. Everything is computed automatically from data the engineers themselves enter daily — no score is manually assigned, which makes the metric objective and auditable.

2. Data sources

The score is built from three independent data streams, stored as version-controlled JSON in the Controls_Team_Tracker repository and updated every working day:

  • Attendance — recorded on the Daily Report page for each working day (Mon–Sat, 6 days).
  • Weekly assignments — every task assigned for the week with its live status (pending / in progress / completed). Assigned by the manager, updated by the engineer.
  • Daily activity log — target tasks and completed activities logged each day — the evidence trail of actual work performed.

3. The weekly scoring formula

Overall Score = (Attendance × 0.40) + (Task Completion × 0.40) + (Activity Log × 0.20)

Component Weight How it is calculated
Attendance 40% Days present ÷ total workdays × 100 (week = Monday–Saturday, 6 days)
Task Completion 40% Tasks marked Completed ÷ total tasks assigned × 100
Activity Log 20% min(log entries ÷ 10 × 100, 100) — ten or more entries in the week scores the full 100%

Why these weights: attendance and task delivery are weighted equally and highest because they directly measure whether project work is being done. The activity log carries lighter weight — it measures diligence in documenting work — but undocumented work cannot be verified, handed over, or audited.

Note: the “Task Rate” column in the Engineer Daily Task Matrix table is a simpler live ratio — (completed tasks + completed projects) ÷ (assigned tasks + projects) — used for the day-to-day view. The weighted weekly score above drives the Star Performer banner.

4. What “Engineers Needing Support” means

Engineers whose completion rate falls below 50% (with at least one task or project assigned) appear in the panel. A low score is not automatically a performance problem. It is a signal that must be diagnosed. The panel now does this automatically — tap any flagged engineer to expand the full justification:

  • Over-allocated — assigned to 2+ concurrent active projects with task completion collapsed. The load exceeds one person’s capacity — this is the pattern that justifies recruiting or outsourcing.
  • Tasks not closing — daily activity is being logged but tasks aren’t reaching completion: likely blockers (materials, site access, dependencies).
  • No logged output — nothing completed and nothing logged; verify logging discipline before drawing any conclusion.
  • Below target — under threshold with no dominant cause; monitor and coach.

5. Worked example

Engineer A (needs support) Engineer B (healthy)
Attendance 5 / 6 days = 83.3% 6 / 6 days = 100%
Task Completion 6 / 15 tasks = 40.0% 9 / 10 tasks = 90.0%
Activity Log 4 entries = 40.0% 11 entries = 100%
Overall Score 33.3 + 16.0 + 8.0 = 57.3 40.0 + 36.0 + 20.0 = 96.0

Engineer A’s breakdown is the key: attendance is nearly perfect, but 15 tasks were assigned in one week and only 6 could be completed. The score is low because the assigned load exceeded one person’s capacity — not because the engineer was absent or idle. This is the justification pattern HR needs to see.

6. Building the HR justification

For each flagged engineer, the expanded panel on the Skill Matrix page shows the component breakdown, active project names, diagnosis and recommendation. The “Copy Justification for HR” button generates a ready-to-paste statement. Alongside it, present:

  • Project load — number of concurrent projects (Team Project Tracker).
  • Task volume trend — assigned vs. completed over the last 4 weeks.
  • Phase criticality — projects in PLC Power Up, IO Check, Trials, FAT or SAT carry contractual, deadline-bound risk.
  • Persistence — a one-week dip is noise; a 4-week trend is structural.

“[Engineer], score [X] for [week]. Attendance [A]%, confirming full availability. Assigned [N] tasks across [P] concurrent projects; completed [C]. Task completion of [T]% has persisted for [W] consecutive weeks, indicating sustained over-allocation rather than underperformance. Projects [names] are in [phase], where delays carry contractual FAT/SAT deadline risk. Recommendation: [recruit one engineer / engage outsourced engineer for N months] to absorb [specific scope], restoring a completable load of ~10 tasks/week.”

7. Recruit vs. outsource — decision guide

Factor Recruit permanent Outsource / contract
Overload duration Low scores persist 8+ weeks across multiple engineers; pipeline growing Tied to 1–2 projects or a peak phase (installation, commissioning)
Skill needed Core skills used on every project (PLC, HMI, electrical design) Niche or one-off skill (specific robot brand, specialised instrumentation)
Number flagged 3+ engineers consistently below threshold 1 engineer below threshold during a project peak
Cost horizon Long-term capacity investment Short-term, ends with the project phase

8. Why this metric is defensible

  • Every input is entered by engineers and managers during normal daily work — nothing is retrofitted for the report.
  • The formula is fixed, published (this article), and applied identically to every engineer.
  • Raw data is version-controlled in GitHub, so any week’s score can be re-derived and audited from commit history.
  • The component breakdown separates capacity problems from performance problems — protecting engineers from unfair conclusions while giving management a precise lever to act on.

posts.author: Admin

posts.content:
Material BOM Tracker — Sample Sheet

Use this template to plan procurement before entering data into the tracker app

Getting PLC, HMI, Servo, and other critical materials on time is essential to completing a project on schedule. This sheet helps you plan out BOM, PR, PO, and Material Receipt dates for every item before logging them into the Material Procurement Tracker.

What's in the sheet

  • 12 sample materials (PLC, HMI, Servo Drive/Motor, Safety Relay, E-Stop, etc.)
  • Columns for BOM Created, PR Created, PR Approved, PO Created, PO Approved, Target Receipt, Actual Receipt
  • A second "Instructions" tab explaining the date format and alert rules

Automatic Alert Rules in the Tracker

  • Red flag — PR Created not filled within 3 days of BOM Created date
  • Red flag — PO Created not filled within 3 days of PR Approved date
  • Red flag — Target Receipt date passed without Actual Receipt logged
  • Amber — Material due within 3 days of Target Receipt

How to use it

  1. Download the sheet below
  2. Fill in your project's material list and dates (YYYY-MM-DD format)
  3. Open the Material Procurement Tracker page
  4. Select or add your project, paste the BOM file's link into "BOM Location"
  5. Manually add each material into the tracker with its dates — the tracker will flag any item that's overdue automatically
